ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, point $G$ is located on $BC$ and $\frac{GC}{BG}=\frac{1}{2}$. Line $DG$ intersects the diagonal $AC$ at point $F$. A perpendicular line from $D$ to $DG$ intersects the extension of line $CA$ at point $E$. If $AE=5$, what is the length of $DF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $EH \perp AD$ through point $E$, extending it to intersect the extended line of $DA$ at $H$,\\
$\therefore \angle H=90^\circ$,\\
In square $ABCD$, $AB=BC=CD=AD$, $\angle BAD=\angle B=\angle BCD=\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 2+\angle 3=90^\circ$, $\angle H=\angle BCD$,\\
Because $DE\perp DG$,\\
$\therefore \angle EDG=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 2+\angle 1=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 3$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DEH\sim \triangle DGC$,\\
$\therefore \frac{EH}{GC}=\frac{DH}{DC}$,\\
Since $\frac{GC}{BG}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ let $GC=x$, then $BG=2x$, $DC=BC=3x$,\\
$\therefore \frac{EH}{GC}=\frac{DH}{3x}$,\\
$\therefore DH=3EH$,\\
Because $AC$ is the diagonal of square $ABCD$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAC=45^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle EAH=\angle DAC=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle HEA=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore EH=HA$,\\
$\therefore EH^2+HA^2=25$,\\
$\therefore EH=HA=\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore DH=3EH=\frac{15\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore AD=DH−AH=5\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore GC=\frac{1}{3}BC=\frac{1}{3}AD=\frac{5\sqrt{2}}{3}$,\\
$\therefore DG=\sqrt{CD^2+CG^2}=\frac{10\sqrt{5}}{3}$,\\
Since in square $ABCD$, $AD\parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \frac{CG}{AD}=\frac{GF}{DF}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
$\therefore DF=3GF$,\\
$\therefore DF=\frac{3}{4}DG=\frac{3}{4}\times \frac{10\sqrt{5}}{3}=\boxed{\frac{5\sqrt{5}}{2}}$;

Thus DF=sqrt((s-3s/4)^2+(s-s/4)^2)=sqrt((s/4)^2+(3s/4)^2)=s sqrt(10)/4. Substituting s=5sqrt(2), get DF=5sqrt(2)*sqrt(10)/4=5sqrt(5)/2.

claims.claim: The equation of the line passing through D and perpendicular to DG is y-s=-(1/3)(x-s).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore, the slope of the line passing through D and perpendicular to DG is -1/3, and its equation is y-s=-(1/3)(x-s)

claims.claim: This perpendicular line intersects the extension line of AC to obtain E=(-s/2,3s/2).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Let it intersect the extension line y=s-x of AC: s-x=s-(x-s)/3, solving gives x=-s/2, y=3s/2, therefore E=(-s/2,3s/2)

claims.claim: From E=(-s/2,3s/2), obtain AE=s/sqrt(2).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Thus the length of AE is sqrt((s/2)^2+(s/2)^2)=s/sqrt(2)

claims.claim: From AE=5, obtain s=5sqrt(2).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Given AE=5, so s=5sqrt(2)

claims.claim: The equation of DG is y=3x-2s.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The equation of DG is y-s=3(x-s), that is y=3x-2s

claims.claim: DG intersects AC to obtain F=(3s/4,s/4).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Intersecting with AC's y=s-x, obtain s-x=3x-2s, so x=3s/4, y=s/4, that is F=(3s/4,s/4)

claims.claim: From D=(s,s) and F=(3s/4,s/4), obtain DF=s sqrt(10)/4.
claims.label: reasoning

claims.claim: Substituting s=5sqrt(2) gives DF=5sqrt(5)/2.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Substituting s=5sqrt(2), gives DF=5sqrt(2)*sqrt(10)/4=5sqrt(5)/2
